narratives.Overview:
## Summary

CodeQL open alert on default branch: **HIGH** `js/bad-tag-filter` — Bad HTML filtering regexp.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Alert | [#143](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/143) |
| Rule | `js/bad-tag-filter` |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Location | `packages/core/src/presentation-ceiling/evaluate.ts` ~L578 |
| Message | This regular expression does not match script end tags like </script\t\n bar>. |

## What to build

Rewrite or bound the flagged site so CodeQL `js/bad-tag-filter` clears for this alert (or document accepted risk with suppress + rationale if false positive after review). Prefer a real fix over suite-config changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CodeQL alert [#143](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/143) clears on master (auto-close or dismiss with reason after fix).
- [ ] Existing unit tests for the touched module still pass; add adversarial input coverage if useful.
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #143.

## Non-goals

- Changing CodeQL suite config as the primary fix.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue (siblings tracked separately).

## In plain English

CodeQL alert #143 flags a HIGH js/bad-tag-filter hit on production presentation-ceiling readerEvidence: the HTML path extracts `script` bodies with an end-tag pattern that misses browser-forgiving closes such as `</script` + whitespace + junk + `>`. Prefer-A hardens that end-tag match so CodeQL clears, keeps the extract-for-static-analysis semantics (this is not a browser XSS sanitizer), adds adversarial coverage, and refuses suite-config or dismiss as the primary fix.

## Proposed Bound remedy (draft — critics refute before bind)

relieves: P1
- In packages/core/src/presentation-ceiling/evaluate.ts readerEvidence (~L578 at dispatch-sha), replace the incomplete end-tag `<\/script\s*>` with a complete end-tag that matches CodeQL's cited shape (at minimum `<\/script\b[^>]*>` so `</script\t\n bar>` matches). Keep start-tag `<script\b[^>]*>`, keep non-greedy body capture, keep joining extracted bodies for downstream JS/TS parse / fallbackReaderEvidence. Do not change the HTML branch's purpose: extract script text for static reader-evidence, not sanitize for browser render.

relieves: P1
- Add or extend unit coverage under packages/core/src/presentation-ceiling/ so an HTML fixture whose script closes as `</script\t\n bar>` (and a normal `</script>`) still yields the expected reader-evidence behavior for that extraction path. Existing module tests stay green.

relieves: P1
- Verification endpoint: CodeQL alert #143 clears on master after the harden lands (Acceptance). Syntactic rewrite alone is not clearance.

relieves: P1

## Reject (draft)

- Changing .github/codeql/codeql-config.yml (or paths-ignore / query suite) as the primary fix.
- Dismissing alert #143 as false-positive without hardening the flagged production site.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts.
- Treating this extractor as a general-purpose HTML sanitizer or pulling a sanitizer library as the default cut unless a later measurement shows the hardened regex still fails CodeQL clearance.
- Widening file_scope past presentation-ceiling evaluate + its tests + CHANGELOG without a new lean.

## file_scope (draft)

- packages/core/src/presentation-ceiling/evaluate.ts
- packages/core/src/presentation-ceiling/* (tests touching readerEvidence / HTML script extract)
- CHANGELOG.md

Round 1, open critique. Reviewed issue body and comments through 6257037912 only; source and contract reads pinned to 8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f.

Prefer-A's local hardening direction is sufficient for P1, with adversarial behavioral tests, CHANGELOG, and actual master CodeQL clearance. The literal proposed minimum needs correction before binding; I do not endorse it unchanged.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: the proposed word boundary can discard reader evidence

Evidence: pinned evaluate.ts:578 extracts script bodies before TypeScript analysis. I reproduced the original and proposed expressions in Node, without modifying the tree. For an actual tab/newline close, the original extracts nothing and the proposed expression correctly extracts the reader. But for:

~~~html
<script>const x="</script-not-a-close>"; readFileSync("CHANGELOG.md");</script>
~~~

The original captures the complete body; the proposed end-tag captures only `const x="`. The word boundary also matches before punctuation such as the hyphen. This is a concrete loss of downstream reader input, conflicting with the draft's preserve-extraction-semantics requirement. On this untrusted-source path, merely satisfying a filtering query must not introduce evidence blindness.

Disposition: retain Prefer-A, but replace its permitted minimum with a delimiter-aware end-tag expression (for example `</script(?=[	
  />])[^>]*>`, subject to CodeQL verification), or an equivalent implementation that preserves the reader in this counterexample. Keep the start-tag and downstream analysis scope unchanged. Bind behavioral coverage for both the cited malformed close and this non-close sentinel, normal closes, and multiple scripts. Use the existing evaluatePresentationCeilingFromSnapshot test harness to assert reader findings, not only regex matches: evaluate.test.ts already has CHANGELOG reader cases and negative source-string cases. This closes the concrete regression without expanding to general HTML parsing.

## F2 — sharpens-framing: distinguish design acceptance from delivered clearance

Evidence: draft 6257027950 correctly says syntactic rewrite alone is not clearance and requires alert #143 to clear on master. Pin-reading and the Node reproduction establish extraction behavior only; neither runs CodeQL or establishes the alert's current state. Failure mode: a green unit suite or merged regex change is recorded as P1 delivered before the default-branch analysis confirms it.

Disposition: preserve the draft's endpoint and record the post-fix master SHA, successful relevant CodeQL analysis, and alert #143 fixed state as delivery evidence. No suite exclusion, suppression, or dismissal should substitute for that result. The lean can bind with this recording clarification; clearance is not claimed by this critique.

## F3 — footnote: dispatch recording inconsistencies

The authoritative envelope ceiling is 6257037912 and was honored. The pinned contract's single-critic Round-1 rule specifies the triage write-back as ceiling when present (6257030572); its post-deposit exception applies to two or more critics. This N=1 envelope instead includes the later deposit. Also, Stop 1 records open critique while carrying a refutation-target; the envelope itself appropriately supplies no named refutation target. These are protocol-recording inconsistencies, not evidence that the product fix fails, and I have not silently re-ceiled or changed the charter. Parent should record their disposition rather than describe the dispatch as exact protocol conformance.

Road not taken: a full HTML parser could supply stronger tokenization semantics, but that adds dependency and integration scope beyond this demonstrated end-tag defect. A sanitizer library addresses a different purpose. Prefer the bounded extractor correction unless behavioral counterexamples or CodeQL results demonstrate that it cannot meet the stated endpoint.

Verification limits: pinned source/contract inspection plus isolated Node regex reproduction; no product edits, module test run, or CodeQL run. This is the one critic post, not synthesis or ingest clearance.

1. F1 is addressed. The pinned readerEvidence at evaluate.ts:578 extracts HTML script bodies, joins them, and sends them into TypeScript reader analysis. The Bound delimiter lookahead accepts the cited end-tag with actual tab/newline and trailing text while rejecting the hyphen after script in </script-not-a-close>. Isolated Node assertions of the proposed extraction expression passed normal close, actual-tab/newline close, the full F1 sentinel body with its subsequent readFileSync("CHANGELOG.md"), and two scripts with the reader in the second body. The unchanged start-tag, non-greedy capture, and join preserve the bounded extraction pipeline. This directly addresses evidence loss from the prior bare word-boundary proposal on untrusted source input.

2. Behavioral coverage is addressed. The Bound names normal closes, the CodeQL-cited close, the F1 sentinel, and multiple scripts, and directs reader-finding assertions through the existing evaluatePresentationCeilingFromSnapshot harness rather than regex-only checks. Pinned evaluate.test.ts already supplies changelog-production-reader and negative source-string cases, so this uses an existing observable behavior and test mechanism. The new HTML fixtures must exercise that path during implementation; the isolated assertions above do not substitute for those tests.

Green unit tests or a syntactic rewrite cannot satisfy that endpoint, and suite exclusions, suppression, and dismissal cannot replace it. The CHANGELOG limb and narrow file scope remain consistent with P1.

A full HTML parser remains a plausible stronger tokenizer, but the demonstrated defect does not require that integration scope. A behavioral counterexample to the bounded remedy or failure to obtain the required CodeQL clearance would justify revisiting that choice; the Bound already retains that contingency.
